title: Verbi Pronominali
subtitle: Farsi, andarsene, cavarsela — idiomatic verbs built from pronoun combinations.
objectives: Recognize pronominal verbs as fixed idiomatic units
Conjugate andarsene and cavarsela correctly across their pronoun set
Use common pronominal verbs naturally in context

content.intro: Pronominal verbs fuse a base verb with one or more pronouns into an idiomatic unit whose meaning often can't be guessed from the parts — a hallmark of fluent, native-sounding Italian.
content.explanation: Andarsene (to leave, to go away) combines the reflexive andarsi with ne, both of which move together through the conjugation. Cavarsela (to get by, to manage) combines cavarsi with la. These aren't literal reflexive/partitive meanings anymore — they're memorized as whole idiomatic verbs.

rules.heading: a) Common pronominal verbs
rules.body:
• farcela — to manage, to make it: Ce l'ho fatta! (I made it!)
  • cavarsela — to get by: Me la cavo bene in inglese. (I get by well in English.)
  • prendersela — to take offense/get upset: Non prendertela! (Don't take it personally!)
  • sentirsela — to feel up to something: Non me la sento di uscire stasera.

rules.heading: b) Passato prossimo of andarsene
rules.body: Takes essere, with the participle agreeing: Se n'è andato. (He left.) Se ne sono andate. (They [f.] left.)

examples.it: Me ne vado, ci vediamo domani.

examples.en: He/she got through the exam really well.

examples.it: Non prendertela, non era colpa tua.
examples.en: Don't take it personally, it wasn't your fault.

commonMistakes.why: Andarsene's pronouns (me/te/se/ce/ve/se + ne) precede the verb as a fixed unit — they can't be reordered or split.
The combined pronoun ce l' comes before the auxiliary, as one fixed sequence.

items.prompt: Sono stanco, ___ vado a dormire. (andarsene, io)
items.explanation: Io form of andarsene: me ne vado.
Ce l'ho fatta — I made it.

options: Don't take it (an object) with you.
Don't take offense / don't be upset about it.
Don't take it away from him.
items.explanation: Prendersela is an idiomatic pronominal verb meaning to take offense/get upset.
Tu form of andarsene: te ne vai.
Lei form of andarsene: se ne va.

items.prompt: Non ___ sento di parlarne ora. (sentirsela, io)
items.explanation: Io form of sentirsela: me la sento.

items.prompt: ___ caviamo bene in situazioni difficili. (cavarsela, noi)
items.explanation: Noi form of cavarsela: ce la caviamo.

items.prompt: Non ___ prendere, era solo uno scherzo! (prendersela, tu, negative imperative)
items.explanation: Tu form of prendersela: te la prendi / non te la prendere.

items.prompt: Finalmente ce l'___ (fare - passato prossimo, loro)
items.explanation: Farcela, loro passato prossimo: ce l'hanno fatta.
Io form of andarsene: me ne vado.
Se n'è andato is the passato prossimo of andarsene.

items.prompt: Which pronominal verb means "to manage/get by"?
items.explanation: Cavarsela means to manage/get by.

items.prompt: Which pronominal verb means "to take offense/get upset"?
items.explanation: Prendersela is the idiomatic verb for taking offense.
Farcela means to manage/make it.

items.prompt: Which auxiliary does andarsene take in the passato prossimo?
items.explanation: Andarsene always takes essere.

items.prompt: "Non me la sento di uscire stasera" means...
options: I don't feel up to going out tonight.
I don't feel it in my hand tonight.
I won't go out with her tonight.
items.explanation: Sentirsela means to feel up to doing something.

items.prompt: Pronominal verbs are best understood as...
options: fixed idiomatic units, not literal reflexive+pronoun combos
random combinations with no fixed meaning
items.explanation: Their meaning often can't be guessed from the individual parts.

items.statement: Andarsene's pronouns can be reordered freely.
items.explanation: They form a fixed sequence (me/te/se/ce/ve/se + ne).
This is farcela's idiomatic meaning.

items.statement: Cavarsela combines cavarsi with the pronoun la.
items.explanation: Cavarsela = cavarsi + la, fused into one idiomatic verb.

items.statement: The participle in andarsene's passato prossimo agrees with the subject.
items.explanation: Se n'è andata shows normal essere-participle agreement.

items.statement: Prendersela is used literally to mean "to take something with you".
items.explanation: It's idiomatic for taking offense/getting upset, not literal.

items.statement: Pronominal verbs are a hallmark of fluent, native-sounding Italian.
items.explanation: They're a genuine marker of advanced fluency.

items.statement: Sentirsela means "to feel up to doing something".
items.explanation: This is exactly its idiomatic meaning.

summary: Pronominal verbs (andarsene, cavarsela, farcela, prendersela) are idiomatic fixed units, not literal reflexive+pronoun combinations.
Their pronoun sequence moves together as a block through the conjugation.
Andarsene takes essere in the passato prossimo, with normal participle agreement.
